difficultyReason: Short stimulus (40 words) with explicit 'therefore' marker followed immediately by the main conclusion. Correct answer paraphrases the conclusion; distractors restate premises.
stimulus: Most plants require sunlight to photosynthesize effectively. Ivy grows well in shade, which means it has adapted to low-light conditions. Therefore, ivy must have a different photosynthetic mechanism than most plants.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main point of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ivy grows well in shaded environments.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most plants require sunlight to photosynthesize.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ivy must employ a different photosynthetic mechanism than most plants do.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Low-light conditions are beneficial for all shade-tolerant plants.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert sunlight into energy.

explanations.correct: The conclusion comes directly after 'therefore' and asserts that ivy must have a different photosynthetic mechanism. Answer C paraphrases this claim without restating premises.
explanations.A: This is a premise presented early in the argument, not the conclusion.
explanations.B: This is the opening premise, not what the author concludes.
explanations.D: This overgeneralizes beyond what the argument claims; it refers to 'all' plants, not just ivy.
explanations.E: This is background context about photosynthesis, not the author's main point.

difficultyReason: Straightforward stimulus (45 words) with 'thus' marker introducing the conclusion. Main point is a simple paraphrase. Distractors misstate intermediate reasoning or background facts.
stimulus: The city's water treatment facility uses outdated filtration methods. These methods fail to remove many harmful microorganisms. Thus, the facility should upgrade to modern filtration technology to protect public health.
questionStem: The main point of the argument is that:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Modern filtration technology is available for water treatment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The water treatment facility currently uses outdated filtration methods.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Public health is an important concern for city officials.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The facility should adopt modern filtration technology to safeguard public health.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Harmful microorganisms exist in untreated water.

explanations.correct: The word 'thus' signals the main conclusion: the facility should upgrade. Answer D paraphrases this recommendation without introducing new claims.
explanations.A: Background fact about what is available, not the author's main point.
explanations.B: A premise presented as background; not what the author concludes.
explanations.C: Implied background assumption, not the author's main claim.
explanations.E: A supporting fact, not the author's main conclusion.

difficultyReason: Short stimulus (38 words) with 'hence' signaling the main conclusion at the end. Clear paraphrase required. Distractors restate supporting claims presented earlier.
stimulus: Novels written in the first person create an intimate connection between reader and narrator. This stylistic choice allows readers to access the narrator's inner thoughts directly. Hence, first-person narrative is an effective literary technique for building reader engagement.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: First-person narrative is the only way to create reader engagement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: First-person narrative is an effective technique for building reader engagement.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Readers prefer direct access to a narrator's inner thoughts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Intimate connection between reader and narrator is always beneficial.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All novels should be written in the first person.

explanations.correct: The conclusion follows 'hence' and asserts that first-person narrative is effective for engagement. Answer B captures this without overstating (e.g., 'only') or understating.
explanations.A: Overstates by inserting 'only'—the argument does not claim this is the sole way.
explanations.C: A supporting premise, not the main conclusion.
explanations.E: Goes beyond the argument, which discusses effectiveness, not prescription for all novels.

difficultyReason: Short stimulus (43 words) ending with 'so' followed by the main conclusion. Correct answer restates the conclusion faithfully. Wrong answers extract premises or misrepresent the scope.
stimulus: Encryption protects digital communications from unauthorized access. Businesses handle sensitive customer data that must be kept confidential. So businesses should use encryption to safeguard customer information.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main point of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Encryption is the only way to protect customer data.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Businesses handle sensitive customer data.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Encryption protects digital communications from unauthorized access.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Businesses should use encryption to protect customer information.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Customer data is always at risk of being stolen.

explanations.correct: The conclusion after 'so' recommends that businesses use encryption. Answer D paraphrases this recommendation directly.
explanations.A: Overstates by claiming encryption is 'the only way'—the argument makes no such exclusive claim.
explanations.B: A supporting premise, not the main conclusion.
explanations.C: A supporting premise used to justify the recommendation.
explanations.E: Not claimed by the argument; the argument focuses on safeguarding, not on risk inevitability.

difficultyReason: Short stimulus (41 words) with 'therefore' preceding the conclusion. Main point is directly stated. Distractors misstate background facts or intermediate reasoning.
stimulus: Pesticide residues accumulate in soil over time. Accumulated pesticide residues harm beneficial soil organisms. Therefore, reducing pesticide use is necessary to maintain soil health.
questionStem: The main point of the argument is that:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pesticide residues accumulate in soil.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reducing pesticide use is necessary to maintain soil health.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Soil organisms are harmed by pesticide residues.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Beneficial organisms are essential for soil function.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pesticides should never be used in agriculture.

explanations.correct: The word 'therefore' introduces the conclusion: reducing pesticide use is necessary for soil health. Answer B captures this exact claim.
explanations.A: A supporting premise presented at the start.
explanations.C: Another supporting premise, not the main conclusion.
explanations.D: Background assumption, not the author's main point.
explanations.E: Overstates the argument, which argues for reduction, not elimination.

difficultyReason: Short stimulus (39 words) with 'it follows that' signaling the main conclusion. Correct answer paraphrases the conclusion. Distractors conflate premises with the conclusion.
stimulus: Antibiotics kill bacteria by targeting their cell walls. Bacteria that have altered cell walls resist these antibiotics. It follows that antibiotic resistance arises when bacteria evolve cellular defenses.
questionStem: Which one of the following most accurately expresses the main conclusion of the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All bacteria are capable of evolving resistance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antibiotics are ineffective against resistant bacteria.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Antibiotic resistance develops when bacteria evolve cellular defenses.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Bacteria have different types of cell walls.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Antibiotics function by destroying bacterial cell structures.

explanations.correct: The phrase 'it follows that' introduces the main conclusion about how antibiotic resistance arises. Answer C faithfully paraphrases this conclusion.
explanations.A: Overgeneralizes; the argument does not claim all bacteria can evolve resistance.
explanations.B: A consequence of resistance mentioned implicitly, but not the main point about how resistance arises.
explanations.D: A supporting premise, not the main conclusion.
explanations.E: A supporting premise explaining how antibiotics work, not what causes resistance.
